# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Harden remaining exec mocks against HERDR_BIN_PATH (match herdr calls by args, not binary name)

## Problem statement

Several worklist test files use `makeExecMock` helpers that match herdr CLI calls with `bin === 'herdr'`. Because `isPaneVisible()` / pane helpers resolve the CLI as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? 'herdr'`, those mocks silently miss whenever the suite runs inside a herdr pane (which sets `HERDR_BIN_PATH` to an absolute path), and the call falls through to the mock's generic branch — which can flip a visibility probe to fail-open 'visible'. This is a latent hermeticity defect discovered while fixing the same issue in WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI (worklist-visibility.test.ts).

## Users

- CI agents and developers running the test suite inside herdr panes
- Automated test infrastructure that inherits `HERDR_BIN_PATH`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 8 identified test files replace `bin === 'herdr' && …` conditions with arg-only matching (matching on `args[0]` / `args[1]` etc. only, no `bin` check), matching the pattern already applied in `worklist-visibility.test.ts`.
2. All related `makeExecMock` functions include a comment explaining why the `bin` name is not matched (referencing WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI).
3. All 8 files listed in the description plus `worklist-active-tab-marker.test.ts` are updated.
4. Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test`) with no regressions.

## Constraints

- No production code changes — test-only fix.
- Do not modify `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (already fixed).
- Preserve existing mock return shapes and behaviour.
- Keep indentation and style consistent with surrounding code.

## Existing state

The following files contain `bin === 'herdr' && …` conditions in their `makeExecMock` helpers:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts:114` — `tab` / `get`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state.test.ts:78` — `pane` / `get`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts:121,200` — `pane` / `get`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts:90` — `pane` / `get`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts:104` — `pane` / `get`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-nested-expand.test.ts:128` — `pane` / `get`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-timeout.test.ts:113,374` — `pane` or `tab`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-active-tab-marker.test.ts:90` — `pane` / `get`

The fix in `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (from WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI) shows the target pattern: remove the `bin === 'herdr'` check entirely and match purely on arguments.

## Desired change

Remove `bin === 'herdr' && ` from each `if` condition in the listed files, matching the fix applied to `worklist-visibility.test.ts`. Add explanatory comments noting the hermeticity rationale.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` — change line 114
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state.test.ts` — change line 78
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — change lines 121, 200
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts` — change line 90
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts` — change line 104
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-nested-expand.test.ts` — change line 128
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-timeout.test.ts` — change lines 113, 374
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-active-tab-marker.test.ts` — change line 90
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — reference for the fixed pattern (already correct)

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI** — Fixed the same issue in `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (the original discovery point)
- **WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3** — Parent work item for the visibility fix series

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** No additional test files need fixing beyond the 8 listed — but the implementer should run a full `grep -rn "bin === 'herdr'"` at the start to confirm.
- **Assumption:** Removing `bin === 'herdr'` does not introduce false-positive matches; the arg patterns are already specific enough (e.g., `args[0] === 'pane' && args[1] === 'get'`).
- **Risk level:** Low — purely test-level changes, no production code touched.

# Record the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract

## Why

The drain-before-cheap feature failed because it hardcoded a cheap-pool budget (2) that no longer matched the proxy config. The cheap pool was silently changed from 2 to 3 slots, and fast is 1 slot -- the inverse of the brief's assumption.

## Scope

- Record the current mode slot counts and where they live:
  - fast = 1 slot (`llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml`: `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; `config-fast.yaml` does not override)
  - cheap = 3 slots (`llm-manager/proxy/config-cheap.yaml`: `session_slot_pool_size: 3`)
- State the contract: client/proxy-consumer logic MUST NOT hardcode pool sizes; derive from live status or not at all.
- Note the change history (cheap 2 -> 3) and the risk of silent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The slot-count contract and both source locations are documented (README or docs/design).
- [ ] A pointer exists from the mode-switch design doc to the contract.
- [ ] No production code change (documentation only).
data.title: Document the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract for client logic

# Differentiate the background of the In Review header

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, all group section headers (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ▼ ──`, `── Idea (2) ──`, `── In Review (5) ──`) are rendered identically — bold, with a foreground stage colour and no background fill. The producer cannot distinguish the In Review section from other sections at a glance, which matters because In Review items are the only ones with an active producer-review obligation. Give the In Review header a grey background so the section stands out visually.

## Users

- **Herdr users (primarily the producer / session operator)** who scan the selection list for the In Review queue and need to locate that section quickly.
  - User story: "As a Herdr user reviewing the selection list, I want the In Review header to have a distinctive grey background so I can spot the review queue section immediately, even when the list is long."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour, e.g. `ANSI.bg(238)` or a nearby grey value) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
2. All other group heading rows (e.g. `Group N`, `Idea`, `Completed`, etc.) are unchanged — no background fill added.
3. The selected-heading highlight still works: when the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing reverse-video selection bar (`reverseWrap`) remains visible on top of the grey background.
4. Heading text, count, collapse arrow, and width-truncation behaviour are unaffected by the background change (single-row heading invariant preserved).
5. Unit tests cover the new rendering: a heading with label `In Review` contains the background escape sequence, and other headings do not; existing heading-render tests still pass.
6. Full project test suite passes with the change.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Use existing ANSI helpers in `worklist.ts` (`ANSI.bg(code)` with a 256-colour code) — no new dependencies.
- Must not change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Implementation must be keyed off the heading's `groupLabel === 'In Review'` (the label originates in `grouping.ts`); keep the label source as the single source of truth.

## Existing state

- Group heading rows are first-class rows in the display-rows model (`DisplayHeadingRow`), interleaved by `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- The heading row is rendered in `createListRenderer` at `worklist.ts:~4482`:
  `const line = `${indent} ${ANSI.fg(stageColor(undefined))}${ANSI.bold}── ${row.groupLabel} (${row.count}) ${arrow} ──${ANSI.reset}``
- `ANSI.bg(code)` exists at `worklist.ts:~345` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`) and is already used for banner fills (e.g. `ANSI.bg(196)`, `ANSI.bg(220)`, `ANSI.bg(40)`).
- The `In Review` group label is assigned in `grouping.ts:~309` (`groupLabel: 'In Review'` for `stage === 'in_review'`).
- Selected rows are wrapped with `reverseWrap` (re-asserts `\x1b[0m` resets to keep the whole selected row highlighted); heading rows have no interior resets so they are handled fine.

## Desired change

- In the heading-row render branch of `createListRenderer`, when `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, wrap the line's base style with a grey background (`${ANSI.bg(238)}` or similar), keeping the existing foreground/bold styling and the existing `reverseWrap` interaction on selection. Other headings render as today.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch (`createListRenderer`, ~line 4482); add conditional grey background for `groupLabel === 'In Review'`; `ANSI.bg` helper at ~line 345.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — extend with tests asserting the background escape sequence on `In Review` headings and its absence on others.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `stageColor`/ANSI conventions (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- Grey background may reduce contrast against the 220 (yellow-ish) foreground `stageColor` for in-review headings; mitigate by choosing a dark grey (238) and verifying readability. If contrast is insufficient, the foreground can be switched to white (231) for this heading only — record the choice in the implementation.
- Selection visibility: reverse-wrap must stay visible over the background — covered by AC3; verify selection rendering in a terminal, not just by string matching.
- Scope creep: do NOT extend the background to other headings unless separately requested — that is a separate work item (recorded here to avoid accidental bundling).
- Test brittleness: assert on the presence of the `\x1b[48;5;...m` background sequence for the In Review heading rather than on exact full-row strings, to avoid coupling to foreground/bold detail changes.

## Related work

- **Duplicate check performed** — no overlapping completed item found. Related completed items (none duplicates): WL-0MS4FIEN40037GB9 (total actionable count in Herdr header), WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB (in_progress/in_review in mandatory In Review set), WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ (selection-list refresh on tab focus), WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 (heading rows as first-class display rows — this feature builds on that model).
- `docs/icons-design.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed description ("make the In Review header background gray (or similar) to differentiate that section from other sections") was specific enough to draft the brief directly. Assumption recorded: "gray (or similar)" means a grey ANSI 256 background (default candidate: 238, same value already used elsewhere in `worklist.ts`), applied only to the In Review heading; other section headers remain unchanged. Rationale: description explicitly scopes differentiation to "that section".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKW1GUSC1DSWYGS** – OpenCode (completed)
- **WL-0ML1LBF6H0NE40RX** – Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes (completed)
- **WL-0ML4DOK1U19NN8LG** – Add wl list --parent <id> for child-only listing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection, similar
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection

# Intake Brief — Herdr: share one in-process SQLite connection per refresh to bound event-loop blocking (WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B)

## Problem statement

The default-view refresh path opens a **fresh** `WorklogDatabase` connection per `withInProcessDb` call — twice per refresh (`fetchActionableCount` + `fetchChildrenForItems` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Because `better-sqlite3` is fully synchronous, each open runs `new Database(...)`, WAL/foreign-key/busy-timeout pragmas, and the `initializeSchema`/`initializeFts` DDL on the **UI event loop** (~46–70 ms on the 100 MB `worklog.db`). Refreshes are occasional after the WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN counter-only-watch fix, so this is a transient pause rather than continuous lag — but when a refresh coincides with typing it breaches the ≤ 100 ms p95 input-lag budget enforced by the responsiveness guards.

## Users

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — they type (search, commands, text input) in the same TUI whose event loop a refresh's synchronous DB open blocks.
  - *As an operator typing a filter, when a watch-triggered refresh lands, I want keystrokes to remain responsive (≤ 100 ms p95 input lag), so a background refresh never makes me miss a keypress.*
- **Herdr maintainers** — they must keep the input-lag budget and the no-stale-cache invariant while the fast path fans out to more read helpers.
  - *As a maintainer, I want at most one in-process connection open per refresh, so the blocking cost is bounded regardless of how many helpers the refresh fans out to.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single in-process `WorklogDatabase` connection is opened per default-view refresh and shared by the actionable-count and expanded-children reads in that refresh; the connection is closed in a `finally` when the refresh completes.
2. No-stale-cache invariant preserved: the shared connection is still closed per refresh (never reused across a refresh boundary), so the store's in-memory query cache can never serve data across a refresh — reads always reflect the latest committed state.
3. The number of in-process DB opens per refresh drops from 2 to 1, verified by an automated test that counts opens while a refresh cycle exercises both `fetchActionableCount` and `fetchChildrenForItems`.
4. The existing responsiveness guards still pass: event-loop delay stays ≤ 100 ms p95 across watch-triggered refreshes (`worklist-watch.test.ts` F5, `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts`), with no flakiness introduced.
5. Fallback behaviour unchanged: whenever an in-process read is not possible (no resolved worklog dir, no SQLite file, `@worklog/shared` unavailable, or an open/read error), each caller still fails open to its existing `wl` spawn path exactly as today.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the no-stale-cache invariant from WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG: never serve from the in-memory query cache across a refresh boundary — close per refresh.
- In-process reads are best-effort and fail-open: open/read failures degrade to the spawn path.
- Do not change `worklist.doRefresh`'s single-flight/trailing-refresh semantics, the typing gate (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH), or the parallel fetch arrangement.
- Keep the lazy constructor import (`loadInProcessDbCtor`) and add no new dependencies.
- Write path and all fallback paths are untouched.

## Existing state

- `withInProcessDb` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~line 510) opens a fresh `WorklogDatabase` (`new Ctor(...)` — synchronous open + pragmas + `initializeSchema`/`initializeFts` DDL), runs `fn`, closes in `finally`. Two helpers use it per refresh: `fetchActionableCount` (~1005) and `fetchChildrenForItems` (~1167).
- `worklist.doRefresh` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~6125) calls the default fetcher, `fetchChildrenForItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, and later `fetchActionableCount` — so each refresh opens two in-process connections sequentially (~92–140 ms of combined blocking open cost on the 100 MB DB).
- Measured evidence: open cost ~46–70 ms each on a 100 MB `worklog.db` (including `initializeSchema`/`initializeFts`); guard budgets are filed as docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md (≤ 2 s watch→refresh, ≤ 100 ms p95 event-loop delay).

## Desired change

Open **one** in-process connection per refresh and share it between the actionable-count and children reads, closing it in a `finally` at the end of the refresh (e.g. a refresh-scoped connection object both helpers consume, or a small fetcher-level entry point). Alternative considered: move the in-process read off the critical render path entirely (worker thread / non-blocking queue) — recorded as an out-of-scope option; single shared connection is the recommended minimal change that preserves all invariants.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `withInProcessDb` (~510), `fetchActionableCount` (~1005), `fetchChildrenForItems` (~1167): add a refresh-scoped shared connection.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` (~6125): coordinate the one-open-per-refresh lifecycle (open once, share, close in `finally`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` — in-process fast-path tests: add the open-count assertion (AC-3).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-watch.test.ts` — F5 event-loop-delay guard must stay green (AC-4).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — event-loop-delay guard (AC-4).
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (+ `tests/bench/herdr-refresh-perf.test.ts`) — refresh benchmark; extend or reuse to confirm open count / latency.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — update the "Cold-refresh cost" section.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — refresh behaviour notes if referenced.

## Related work

- WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN — parent: *Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item updates* (completed)
- WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG — *Cut cold refresh cost* (completed) — introduced `withInProcessDb` and the no-stale-cache invariant
- WL-0MV5CBO820024S5A — *Watch/refresh verification harness and benchmark* (completed)
- WL-0MUY1CZES0099A04 — *Herdr: UI responsiveness regression test* (completed)
- WL-0MV5CBQTS008ZWHR — *Input responsiveness regression guard* (completed)
- WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S — *Herdr in-process memoization for identical fetches* (completed)
- WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C — *Herdr worklist: add in-flight guard to doRefresh* (completed)
- Docs: `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md`

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption:** sharing one open is safe for the two read helpers because they never mutate and run in the same refresh scope; verified by the open-count test.
- **Risk — subtle connection sharing bug:** a helper that still opens its own connection would silently keep the 2-open behaviour. Mitigation: the open-count assertion in AC-3.
- **Risk — test timing/flakiness:** adding an open-counter/spy must not make the responsiveness guards flaky. Mitigation: assert on open count, not wall-clock, and reuse the existing real-timer patterns from the F5 test.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the off-critical-path (worker) redesign and any connection pooling are out of scope; if they land they get their own work items. (WL-0MQPQP15S003PE9Y already covers general phase-5 pooling discussion — not re-done here.)

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MR269PDL002X882** – Impl: Retry Loop Engine with Dispatch (completed)
- **WL-0MSIG3RL1006AQID** – Wiring, fallback orchestration, lifecycle cleanup (completed)
- **WL-0MSIG3G2X007RAEL** – events.ts: HerdrEventSubscriber socket module (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mv02va29009wben, actionable, better, blocking, blocks, bound, boundary, budget, cache, call, children, close, closing, connection, continuous, count, counter, critical, default, event, fetchactionablecount, fetchchildrenforitems, finally, fix, fresh, herdr, including, input, invariant, keep, lag, loop, memory, move, never, off, one, open, opens, operation, path, process, producer, query, read, reading, reads, refresh, refreshes, rejection, render, serve, share, sqlite, sqlite3, stale, still, store, strict, synchronous, transient, tui, twice, typing, view, watch, when, worklogdatabase

- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mv02va29009wben, actionable, better, blocking, blocks, cache, call, children, close, closing, connection, count, critical, default, event, fix, fresh, herdr, including, input, invariant, keep, lag, loop, memory, move, never, off, one, open, opens, path, process, producer, query, read, refresh, refreshes, rejection, render, serve, share, stale, still, store, transient, tui, twice, view, watch, when


## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the item's discovery context (problem, root cause, measured open cost, recommended approach, invariant to preserve) sufficed to draft this brief.
